papers.title: Faster Algorithms for Triangle-Count Flow
papers.abstract: Sketching compresses a stream into small space while preserving a target statistic. Existing structures support updates in $O(\sqrt{n})$ amortised time but degrade badly in the worst case. We reduce from set disjointness and analyse the communication cost of the induced protocol. Any one-pass algorithm requires $\Omega(n/\log n)$ bits, separating it from the two-pass case. The improvement is the first for sparse graphs since the original interior-point reduction.

papers.title: Evaluating Morphological Bias Faithfulness
papers.abstract: Compositional generalisation asks whether a model that has seen the parts can handle an unseen combination. Aggregate benchmark scores hide large differences between typologically distant languages. We construct a controlled evaluation set covering eleven languages with matched sentence lengths and frequency profiles. Scores range from $84.1$ to $52.7$ across languages, and the gap correlates with morphological complexity ($r = -0.71$). Reporting a single aggregate number is misleading for this class of model, and the per-language breakdown is cheap to add.

papers.title: Detecting Shuffled Supply-Chain Tampering
papers.abstract: Differential privacy bounds what an adversary can learn about any single record. Composition bounds are loose, so deployments spend far more of their budget $\varepsilon$ than necessary. We model the protocol in the applied pi-calculus and discharge the obligations with an automated prover. The bound reduces the required noise by $23\%$ at $\varepsilon = 1$ for the composition depths used in practice. The saving translates directly into utility at a fixed privacy budget.

duplicateVariants.title: Celestial Amplitudes for Asymptotically AdS Scattering
duplicateVariants.abstract: Effective field theories organise quantum corrections as an expansion in $1/\Lambda$. Existing results break down once the coupling $\lambda$ leaves the perturbative regime. We construct the effective action to two loops and resum the leading logarithms with the renormalisation group. The spectrum organises into a discrete family labelled by $\Delta_n = \Delta_0 + 2n + O(\lambda^2)$. The result gives a concrete check of the duality outside the supergravity approximation.

duplicateVariants.title: Thresholds for Sparse Subgraphs
duplicateVariants.abstract: Ramsey theory asks how large a structure must be before order appears in every colouring. The extremal number $\mathrm{ex}(n, F)$ is unknown for the family considered here even up to a constant. We combine a spectral argument with a careful second-moment computation. We prove $\mathrm{ex}(n, F) = \left(\tfrac{1}{2} + o(1)\right)\binom{n}{2}$, matching the conjectured constant. The method removes the degeneracy hypothesis and so applies to a substantially larger family. A typo in the statement of the main theorem has been corrected in this version.

duplicateVariants.title: Scaling  Laws  for  Overparameterised  Models.
duplicateVariants.abstract: Contrastive objectives learn representations by pulling together views of the same input. Uniform-convergence bounds are vacuous once the parameter count exceeds the sample size $n$. We run a controlled study across five environments with matched interaction budgets and three seeds each. The generalisation gap scales as $O(\sqrt{r_{\mathrm{eff}}/n})$ with the effective rank, not the parameter count. The ablation identifies a single cheap component that accounts for most of the robustness.
